questions: Can a path of length K consist of K+1 vertices connected by K edges, or does it mean K vertices connected by K-1 edges?
Are the vertices in each row of matrix P required to be distinct, or can a vertex appear multiple times within the same path?
Can two different paths in the decomposition share vertices or edges, or must all paths be vertex-disjoint and edge-disjoint?
Is the tree rooted at a specific vertex, or can paths start and end at any vertices in the tree?
When K=1, does this mean each path consists of a single vertex with no edges, and how should such paths be represented in the matrix?
For the case where N=1 and K=1, should the output be "Yes" if the tree consists of exactly one vertex?
Are self-loops or multiple edges between the same pair of vertices allowed in the input, even though it's specified as a tree?
What is the expected behavior when NK=1 (i.e., a single vertex tree) - should this always output "Yes" or does it depend on the values of N and K?

Yes. The matrix P must contain each vertex exactly once, forming a permutation of 1 to NK with no repetitions or omissions.

inline_prompts:
You are given a tree with NK vertices. The vertices are numbered 1,2,\dots,NK, and the i-th edge (i=1,2,\dots,NK-1) connects vertices u_i and v_i. This question addresses a different ambiguity not covered in the reference. Determine whether this tree can be decomposed into N paths, each of length K. More precisely, determine whether there exists an N \times K matrix P satisfying the following:
- For each i=1,2,\dots,N and j=1,2,\dots,K-1, there is an edge connecting vertices P_{i,j} and P_{i,j+1}.
Input
The input is given from Standard Input in the following format:
N K
u_1 v_1
u_2 v_2
\vdots
u_{NK-1} v_{NK-1}
Output
If it is possible to decompose the tree into N paths each of length K, print Yes. 
Constraints
- 1 \leq N
- 1 \leq K
- NK \leq 2 \times 10^5
- 1 \leq u_i < v_i \leq NK
- The given graph is a tree.
- All input values are integers.
